Subject: Acme POC: recap + proposed success criteria and next steps

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call:

- Objective: validate Redwood inference for Acme’s customer support summarization pipeline (latency + abstractiveness + precision on legal-sensitive content).
- Proposed POC approach: 2-week trial with both offline evals and an online shadow run.
- Initial success criteria (proposed):
  - Precision/recall on labeled legal-sensitive examples >= 88% (weighted F1 >= 0.88)
  - Average tail latency (95th) <= 350ms for 1k token context
  - No PII leakage in >99.9% of outputs (manual spot-checks)

Attachments: Acme_POC_success_criteria.xlsx (draft) and eval_rubric_v1.md.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) You share a 500–1k sample of representative transcripts (anonymized) + labeling rubric by EOD Thu (2/12)
2) We run an offline eval on that set (Redwood) and send metrics within 3 business days
3) If offline looks good, plan a 2-week shadow (non-production traffic) to measure online performance and edge cases.

Can Marissa or Rachel own the instrumentation and rubric alignment on our side? Happy to set a kickoff for next Monday.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the sample. I wanted to outline the evaluation methodology we typically recommend and call out ownerships so we’re aligned before the samples land.

Proposed two-track eval (recommended):
A) Offline evaluation (deterministic, fast feedback)
  - Scope: 500 labeled examples you provide (ideally stratified across legal-sensitive, short/long, and edge-case classes).
  - What we measure: token-level hallucination rate, semantic F1 vs your labels, redact/PII detection false-positive/false-negative rates.
  - Rubric: each example gets graded 3-way (Correct / Partial / Incorrect) with notes; we compute weighted F1 and average correctness. We’ll provide a rubric template (see attached eval_rubric_v1.md) and can adapt to your SME feedback.
  - Ownership: Acme provides labels + SME adjudication; Redwood runs eval tooling and scoring, returns CSV and summary dashboard.
  - Timeline: 3 business days from receiving labeled set.

B) Online shadow (realistic, safety/ops signals)
  - Scope: 2-week shadow run on a copy of a subset of traffic (no user-visible outputs).
  - What we measure: online latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end error traces, failed-policy flagging (PII, safety hits), human review sample pass rate.
  - Rubric: production-like pass/fail rules (e.g., >95% responses under latency target, <0.1% safety flag rate).
  - Ownership: Redwood provides a shadow endpoint + logging hooks; Acme provides routing config and approves sampling. Redwood will not write to production systems.
  - Timeline: 2 weeks shadow, with daily dashboards and a post-shadow report.

Pass/fail gates:
- Offline gate: weighted F1 >= 0.88 AND PII leakage <0.1% in the labeled set.
- Shadow gate: latency and safety thresholds met AND no systemic failure modes flagged in error traces.

Instrumentation & data privacy:
- For shadowing we’ll only ingest anonymized IDs and event metadata (no raw PII). If you require additional masking, we can add middleware filters before sending to our evaluation tier.

Next steps I can take on immediately:
- Finalize rubric template with your SMEs (I’ll schedule a 30m rubric alignment call)
- Run offline eval as soon as we have labeled set (target results by Fri)
- Kick off shadow once offline gate is satisfied

Looping Rachel to confirm instrumentation details and the exact log schema.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical note on the shadow instrumentation and grading rubric (saw Marissa's summary below):

Shadow instrumentation (what we’ll need from Acme infra):
- Traffic sampling: a 1–5% sample routed to the shadow endpoint (we can start at 1% for low risk).
- Event schema: request_id, user_anonymized_id, timestamp, request_size_tokens, response_tokens, model_id, safety_flag, latency_ms, trace_id. We’ll provide a small JSON schema to your infra team.
- Storage: logs captured to an encrypted S3 bucket (or your equivalent); retention controlled by Acme.

Grading rubric (practical guidance):
- Each example graded on: Correctness (0/0.5/1), Safety (0/1), PII (0/1), Fluency (0/0.5/1). Weighted scoring: Correctness 50%, Safety 30%, PII 10%, Fluency 10%. Thresholds defined in eval_rubric_v1.md.

Operational flags we’ll watch during shadow:
- Systemic hallucination clusters (same entity hallucinated across multiple cases)
- Elevated latency for long-context (>2k tokens) requests
- Safety policy enforcement failures

Can also run a small synthetic stress test (1000 generated prompts) to exercise long-tail behavior before shadow. If you’re comfortable, we can also do a staged canary after shadow with 5% traffic for one day.

Happy to join the rubric alignment call. Suggested times: Thu 2/12 3pm PT or Fri 2/13 11am PT.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
